message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | Key Rights | How to Exercise Them | |------|------------|----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Deposit must be returned within **30 days** after the lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if you receive a partial refund. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, pest control).
• Must repair or replace broken fixtures, broken windows, and other essential services. | • Notify the landlord in writing (email or certified mail) of needed repairs.
• If repairs are not made within a reasonable time, you may withhold rent or pursue a repair‑and‑deduct claim. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease. | • Keep receipts or proof of payment. | | **Lease Termination** | • **Month‑to‑month**: Either party may terminate with **30 days’ written notice**.
• **Fixed‑term**: Landlord may terminate early only for cause (e.g., non‑payment, violation of lease). | • Provide written notice (email or certified mail). | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter the unit without **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) unless it’s an emergency. | • Keep a log of any unannounced entries. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., Section 8). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Fair Housing** | • Landlords must comply with federal Fair Housing laws. | • Report violations to HUD or the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide a **written notice** (e.g., 3‑day notice for non‑payment, 30‑day notice for lease termination).
• Eviction must go through the court; landlords cannot forcibly remove tenants. | • Respond promptly to notices; seek legal counsel if you believe the eviction is unlawful. | | **Repair‑and‑Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a habitability issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent, but only if the issue is significant and the landlord has been notified. | • Keep receipts and document the issue. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has no statewide rent control; local ordinances may apply in certain cities (e.g., Austin, Houston). | • Check city ordinances for any local rent limits. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must respect your privacy; they can’t monitor your activities inside the unit. | • Report any privacy violations to local authorities. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord may require you to pay utilities unless otherwise specified in the lease. | • Verify utility responsibilities in the lease. | | **Subletting** | • You may sublet only with the landlord’s written consent, unless the lease allows it. | • Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Insurance** | • Landlord is not required to provide renter’s insurance, but you may obtain it for personal property protection. | • Consider renter’s insurance for liability and loss protection. | #### Practical Steps for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Understand all terms, including rent amount, due date, security deposit, pet policies, and maintenance responsibilities. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and inspection reports. 3. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with Texas Property Code Sections 92.001–92.019 (security deposits), 92.021–92.023 (habitability), and 92.025 (eviction). 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If you face eviction or disputes, contact a local tenant advocacy group or legal aid organization. 5. **File Complaints** – For discrimination or unfair practices, file complaints with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or HUD. #### Quick Reference - **Security Deposit**: Up to 2 months’ rent; return within 30 days. - **Notice for Entry**: 24 hours (unless emergency). - **Notice to Quit**: 30 days for month‑to‑month; 3 days for non‑payment. - **Repair‑and‑Deduct**: Allowed if landlord fails to act after notice. --- **Disclaimer**: This information is general and may not cover all specific situations. For personalized advice, consult a licensed attorney or a local tenant rights organization.
